question: At what age did Gautama Buddha attain Enlightenment (Nirvana) at Bodh Gaya in Bihar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**35 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment, also known as Nirvana, at the age of **35 years**.
 
• He attained Enlightenment under the **Bodhi Tree** in Bodh Gaya, located in the present-day state of Bihar, India.
 
• After years of meditation and ascetic practices, he realized the **Four Noble Truths**, which became the foundation of Buddhism.
 
• The event of Enlightenment is considered one of the most significant moments in Buddhist tradition and marks the beginning of his journey as the Buddha (the Enlightened One).
 
• The date of his Enlightenment is celebrated as **Buddha Purnima**, observed annually by Buddhists worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Four Noble Truths**

 
 
• The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddha's teachings: the truth of suffering, the truth of the origin of suffering, the truth of the cessation of suffering, and the truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.
 
• These truths explain the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth (samsara) and how one can escape it.
 
 
 
• **Bodhi Tree**
 
 
• The Bodhi Tree under which Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment is a sacred fig tree (Ficus religiosa).
 
• It is considered a major pilgrimage site for Buddhists and is located in the Mahabodhi Temple complex in Bodh Gaya.
 
 
 
• **Nirvana**
 
 
• Nirvana is a state of liberation and freedom from the cycle of birth and rebirth.
 
• It is achieved by understanding the true nature of reality, breaking free from desires, and following the Eightfold Path.
 
 
 
• **Eightfold Path**
 
 
• The Eightfold Path is a set of practices that lead to liberation, including right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.
 
• It serves as the practical guide for ethical conduct, mental discipline, and wisdom in Buddhism.
